title: Eating is becoming an occasion-and-channel system shaped by budget, convenience, identity and where food is consumed
geography: United States food, beverage, retail and foodservice consumption

observations.period: 2026 report overview; U.S. food and beverage consumption

denominator.unit: dollars of spending covered by the report overview

spending_scope.unit: U.S. food and beverage spending represented in report scope

occasion_scope.unit: eating and drinking occasions represented in report scope

decision_system.value: The report frames what, when, where and why Americans eat and drink as a connected consumer-decision system spanning food, beverage, retail and foodservice.

observations.method: Circana commercial market-intelligence report overview drawing on multiple integrated datasets; the public page states market scope but does not expose the full tables, sampling, weighting or model specification.
observations.uncertainty: The spending and occasion figures describe the report's coverage, not a causal estimate or proof that every consumption decision is observed with equal completeness; the public overview does not show uncertainty intervals.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers, households, food and beverage categories, foodservice operators, retailers, manufacturers and channels of consumption.
observations.counterinterpretation: A very large measurement frame can reveal system-level shifts while still obscuring household inequality, cultural meaning, unpaid preparation, food insecurity and the reasons behind individual choices.

observations.period: 2026 report overview; in-home and away-from-home eating

context_split.value: The report explicitly connects in-home and away-from-home eating and drinking rather than treating grocery and foodservice as separate consumer worlds.

occasion_logic.value: Consumption occasions are presented as the unit through which behaviors, channels and opportunities can be compared.

household_tradeoff.value: The source creates an open route for analyzing how money, time, convenience, sociality and preparation effort move consumers between home and away-from-home contexts.

observations.method: Public description of Circana's integrated food, beverage, foodservice, distribution, appliance and housewares datasets.
observations.uncertainty: The overview does not disclose the observed share, frequency or causal drivers of home versus away-from-home substitution, nor how patterns vary by income, age, place or household structure.
observations.subgroup: Households managing food budgets and preparation time, foodservice users, retailers, restaurants, delivery and takeout channels, and consumers whose routines vary by work or care schedules.
observations.counterinterpretation: The home/away distinction may understate hybrid forms such as meal kits, prepared grocery, workplace food, communal cooking and informal food exchange.

observations.period: 2026 report overview; emerging behaviors, segments and channels

early_signal.value: The report is designed to identify emerging eating and drinking behaviors before they become mainstream.

segment_channel.value: It directs attention to occasions, consumer segments and channels with the greatest commercial potential.

mainstreaming.value: Food trends are treated as movements through discovery, occasion, channel and repeat consumption rather than as isolated product preferences.

observations.method: Circana's public commercial framing of the report's use for innovation, marketing, merchandising and activation.
observations.uncertainty: The public overview does not identify which specific behaviors are emerging, their prevalence, persistence, cultural origin or conversion into repeat purchase; it is a report description rather than the full findings.
observations.subgroup: Early adopters, mainstream consumers, culturally distinct food audiences, retailers, brands, foodservice operators and channel intermediaries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Commercial attention to what may become mainstream can amplify novelty and profitable segments while overlooking low-margin routines, food access, health consequences and practices that resist marketization.

dataset_integration.value: The public page says the report integrates datasets spanning food and beverage, foodservice, broadline distribution, small appliances and housewares.

system_boundary.value: Food choice is measured as connected to retail, service, preparation equipment and distribution infrastructure, not only to a packaged product purchase.

power_question.value: The integrated view raises a cross-source question about who controls visibility and value across the eating system: households, brands, retailers, restaurants, platforms or distributors.

observations.method: Circana public description of multiple integrated commercial datasets and its use for innovation, merchandising and activation decisions.
observations.uncertainty: The public page does not disclose dataset overlap, harmonization, coverage bias, ownership, access rules, or whether the integrated view can distinguish correlation from causal influence.
observations.subgroup: Consumers, households, manufacturers, retailers, foodservice operators, distributors, appliance and housewares firms, and data or platform intermediaries.
observations.counterinterpretation: Integration may improve visibility across channels but can also reproduce commercial categories and make unmonetized, informal or culturally specific food practices less visible.

related_sources.claim: Circana's official consumer and market measurement platform.
Official public overview stating the 2026 report's U.S. spending and occasion scope, in-home/away-from-home coverage and integrated dataset frame.

boundary: This record adds an everyday food-culture and consumption-system layer. It treats Circana's public page as a commercial report overview: the page establishes the measurement scope and analytical frame, but does not disclose the full findings, sampling, weighting, category tables, household distribution, causal mechanisms or food-security outcomes.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: The official Circana page was reviewed for the 2026 publication date, 41st-edition claim, 1.8 trillion dollars of spending, 618 billion eating and drinking occasions, in-home and away-from-home scope, emerging-behavior/occasion/channel frame and integrated dataset description.
